question.knowledge_point: Writing a Complex Number in Exponential Form
question.problem: Write the complex number $z=-2+2\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}$ in exponential form.
question.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{(2\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the second quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})| \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=4$ and $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=4\,{\text{e}}^{2\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$
